claim.statement: Kimera-SWM has TWO parallel inquiry/dissonance-detection systems operating at different levels: (1) the IN-LOOP detector — Walker M3 ROLLBACK gate, triggered by hallucinating == True (Allan deviation slope > 0 on gamma phase). This detects when the REASONING ACT is unstable, every 10 ticks. (2) the OUT-OF-LOOP detector — Zetetic Unit, triggered by concept-pair proximity-resonance mismatch. This detects when CONCEPT PAIRS are dissonant in the embedding+prime space, per cycle. They sample different things and do not communicate. M.46 F2's discontinuity-detector behavior at M3 selective halts is system (1); the 6-DissonanceType taxonomy is system (2).
claim.operationalization: Compare the two systems' inputs and outputs: M3 input = gamma phase samples; M3 output = hallucinating boolean; M3 trigger = Allan dev slope > 0. Zetetic input = concept pair + embeddings + primes; Zetetic output = DissonanceLocus + ExplorationStrategy; Zetetic trigger = proximity high + resonance low. Different signals, different consumers, no shared state.
claim.h0: Kimera has only one dissonance-detection system
claim.h1: Kimera has two parallel dissonance-detection systems at different levels

preregistration.analysis_plan: Compare M3 ROLLBACK gate against Zetetic unit; verify non-overlap.

verdict.reasoning: System (1) is in the reasoning pipeline (M.48 rule M3, cognitive_rhythm.py:536, 690-692). System (2) is the zetetic unit (semantic_zetetic_unit.py). They have non-overlapping inputs (gamma phase vs concept embeddings), non-overlapping outputs (boolean vs typed locus), and non-overlapping triggers. They do not communicate. This is a substantive architectural observation: the substrate has redundant inquiry capacity at different abstraction levels. Constructive implication: a future integration could route zetetic dissonance findings into the oscillator (e.g., trigger M4 annealing on STRUCTURAL_TENSION) — making zetetic close the loop.
